title: From docker run to a process
dek: A container is an ordinary Linux process, and docker run is five programs passing it along. This first part of a four-part teardown follows one docker run -it alpine sh through Docker Engine 29.9.2: five API calls on three connections, a create that only writes JSON, a start that rebuilds the whole OCI spec, a shim that daemonises itself and adopts the container, runc building namespaces in C before Go boots, a FIFO that holds the process while dockerd plugs in the network, and the exit status climbing back through three protocols.
byline: 23 October 2026 · Subject: moby@0367cbeb (Docker Engine 29.9.2) and runc v1.5.2 · Part 1 of 4 · Read from the source and the specs; measured where this machine allows
description: Docker Engine 29.9.2 taken apart, part 1: the docker run call sequence, OCI spec generation, containerd and the runc-v2 shim, runc's nsexec stages and 40-byte bootstrap message, the create/start FIFO, and the exit path.
og_description: Part 1 of a four-part Docker teardown at moby 0367cbeb (Engine 29.9.2): docker run as five API calls on three connections (real CLI against a mock daemon), create as bookkeeping and start as a full OCI spec rebuild with 14 capabilities and a private time namespace, the shim that becomes the container's subreaper, runc's three cloned nsexec stages, the exec.fifo barrier that lets dockerd wire the network, and how an exit code climbs back up.
